viperfish: A scientific field-guide illustration of a viperfish in strict side profile, head to the left, its long slender body held in ONE STRONG S-CURVE that dips down behind the head and rises again toward the tail. Its flanks are DARK BOTTLE-GREEN TO BLACK and covered in LARGE HEXAGONAL SCALES set in regular rows, each scale outlined so the whole body reads as a coarse honeycomb mesh. ALONG THE LOWER EDGE OF EVERY SCALE ROW SITS A TINY ROUND GOLD-YELLOW LIGHT, so fine dotted gold lines run the length of the flank and belly. ITS MOUTH GAPES WIDE and is the point: the jaws are lined with LONG THIN WHITE NEEDLE FANGS of uneven length that are too long to close inside it and stand out past the lips in a bristling fringe, and the inside of the mouth is BRIGHT RED. FROM ITS BACK IMMEDIATELY BEHIND THE HEAD, well clear of the jaws, RISES ONE VERY LONG BARE BLACK FILAMENT, thin as a hair, which arches UP AND FORWARD OVER THE TOP OF THE HEAD and ends in a fine tip beyond the snout. Nothing hangs from its chin. Small pale translucent fins with visible rays sit low on the body and at the tail.
commonfangtooth: A scientific field-guide illustration of a common fangtooth in strict side profile, head to the left. ITS PROPORTIONS ARE THE POINT: the whole fish is SHORT AND DEEP, only ABOUT TWICE AS LONG AS IT IS DEEP, a stubby blunt wedge that is deepest just behind the head and narrows quickly to a short tail stock. THE HEAD FILLS THE FRONT HALF OF THE ANIMAL, enormous and steep, its front almost vertical, with deep hollows and low bony ridges scored across the cheek and brow. THE MOUTH IS OPEN AND THE LOWER JAW IS HUGE, hinged far back beneath the eye and dropped wide, carrying TWO ENORMOUS CURVED PALE FANGS at the front that rise well above the upper jaw, each one about as long as the head is deep, with smaller teeth behind. ITS EYE IS SMALL, ROUND AND PALE MILKY BLUE-WHITE with a dark rim, set high and far forward. The skin is DARK CHOCOLATE-BROWN, dull and roughly pitted all over. Its fins are BRISTLY: the rays along the back, belly and tail stand out as separate stiff pale spines with little membrane between them, and the small tail is a spread fan of the same bare rays.
